hints: Look closely at the shape of the leaf in P (rolled up) versus Q (flat and open) and remember what a xerophyte like marram grass does when water is scarce.
Focus on layer X on the inner surface. Think about how loss of water from those hinge cells changes turgor, plasmolysis, and solute concentration, and therefore water potential.
walkthrough:
**Observe what P and Q show**

P is tightly rolled inwards, Q is flat and open. In xerophytes, rolling closes the stomata inside a humid pocket to reduce transpiration.

Rolling is caused by water loss from the large thin-walled cells in layer X, so P is the dry, water-stressed condition and Q is the well-watered condition.

**Apply water relations to layer X**

When cells in X lose water by osmosis, turgor pressure falls and the vacuole and cytoplasm shrink away from the wall. That is plasmolysis.

Losing water also concentrates solutes, so solute potential becomes more negative:
$$\Psi = \Psi_{s} + \Psi_{p}$$
Lower $\Psi_{s}$ plus lower $\Psi_{p}$ means overall water potential $\Psi$ becomes more negative in P than in Q.

**Test statements 1 to 4**

Statement 1 is true: cells in P have lost water, so more negative water potential than in Q.

Statement 2 is true: more water loss means more cells plasmolysed in P.

Statement 3 is false: cells are less turgid in P, not in Q. Statement 4 is false: living leaf cells contain solutes, so water potential stays negative and does not become zero in Q.

options.A: Includes 1 and 2 which are correct, but also includes 3 which is backwards. Cells are less turgid in P, the rolled dry leaf, not in Q.
options.B: Correctly selects only 1 and 2. In P the X cells have lost water, so water potential is more negative and more cells are plasmolysed than in Q.
options.C: Includes 2 which is correct, but also includes 4 which is wrong. Water potential of these cells remains negative in Q due to solutes, it does not become zero.
options.D: Both 3 and 4 are incorrect. Turgidity is lower in P not Q, and water potential does not become zero in Q.
